question: __________ Directive principles of State Policy were added to the Indian Constitution by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act of 1976.
solution:
The correct answer is **__Four__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

**Four Directive** Principles of State Policy were added to the Indian Constitution by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act of 1976.

__
 
• Article 39A – Equal justice and free legal aid.
 
• Article 43A – Participation of workers in the management of industries.
 
• Article 48A – Protection and improvement of the environment and safeguarding of forests and wildlife.
 
• Article 39(f) – Protection of children and youth from exploitation and moral and material abandonment (added to modify Article 39).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP)**

 
 
• The Directive Principles of State Policy are guidelines or principles given to the federal institutes governing the state of India, to be kept in consideration while framing laws and policies.
 
• They are enumerated in Part IV of the Constitution from Articles 36 to 51.
 
• The principles aim to create social and economic conditions under which the citizens can lead a good life.
 
• They are non-justiciable in nature, meaning they are not enforceable by any court, but the principles laid down are considered fundamental in the governance of the country.
 
 
 
• **42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976**
 
 
• Also known as the "Mini-Constitution", this amendment brought about significant changes to the Indian Constitution.
 
• It attempted to reduce the powers of the Supreme Court and High Courts and gave Parliament unlimited power to amend the Constitution, among other changes.
 
• It also added ten Fundamental Duties to the Constitution.
 
• Many of its provisions were later repealed by the 44th Amendment Act of 1978.
